title: Quickly Slice Sweet Potatoes for Low‑Calorie Chips
keyword: how to slice sweet potatoes for chips
meta_description: Learn how to slice sweet potatoes for chips perfectly every time. Get restaurant-thin, crispy results with our best slicing tips and tool guides.
html:
There is nothing more frustrating than a batch of sweet potato chips where half are burnt to a crisp and the other half are soggy, limp fries. The secret to that addictive, salty crunch isn't actually the oven temperature or the type of oil—it's the thickness of the slice. If you want a low-calorie snack that actually satisfies, you need absolute consistency.

Learning how to slice sweet potatoes for chips effectively can be the difference between a kitchen fail and a professional-grade snack. While a chef's knife works in a pinch, achieving a uniform 1/16th-inch thickness by hand is nearly impossible and incredibly tedious. That is where the right gear comes into play.

The Secret to Consistency: Using a Mandoline Slicer

To get that airy, crisp texture, you need slices that are translucent. This is where a Mandoline Slicer becomes your best friend in the kitchen. Unlike a knife, which creates a wedge shape (thicker on one side, thinner on the other), a mandoline ensures every single chip is the exact same thickness.

Using a Mandoline Slicer allows you to achieve restaurant-thin, even slices of veggies and fruit fast. Because these are adjustable mandolines with hand guards, you can dial in the precise thickness for sweet potatoes—usually the thinnest setting—without risking your fingertips. When every slice is identical, they all cook at the same rate, eliminating the "burnt and raw" gamble.

Step-by-Step: How to Slice Sweet Potatoes for Chips

Before you start slicing, prep your potatoes to ensure the best results. Sweet potatoes can be slippery, so a few prep steps make the process safer and faster.

  1. Scrub and Trim: Wash your sweet potatoes thoroughly. You can leave the skin on for extra nutrients and a rustic look, or peel them for a more traditional chip. Trim the ends off to create a flat surface.
  2. Set Your Thickness: Adjust your Mandoline Slicer to the thinnest setting. For low-calorie chips, the thinner the slice, the less oil you'll need to get them crispy.
  3. Secure the Guard: Always use the provided hand guard. Sweet potatoes harden as you reach the end of the root, and the guard keeps your fingers safely away from the blade.
  4. Glide and Slice: Hold the potato firmly against the guard and slide it across the blade in a smooth, steady motion.
  5. Collect and Soak: Collect your slices in a bowl of cold water for 30 minutes. This removes excess starch, which is the key to preventing the chips from sticking together.

Pro Tips for Low-Calorie Crunch

Once you've mastered how to slice sweet potatoes for chips, the goal is to keep the calories low without sacrificing the crunch. Avoid deep frying; instead, opt for the oven or an air fryer.

Pat your slices completely dry with a lint-free towel after soaking. If the slices are damp, they will steam instead of crisp. Lightly mist them with an olive oil spray rather than tossing them in a bowl of oil. This ensures a thin, even coating that saves dozens of calories per serving.

Arrange the slices in a single layer. Overlapping is the enemy of the chip; if they touch, they create soft spots. If you have a lot of potatoes, bake them in batches. It takes longer, but the result is a professional-grade snap.

Maintaining Your Slicing Tools

A dull blade is a dangerous blade. Because sweet potatoes are denser than cucumbers or zucchini, they can put more stress on your equipment. To keep your Mandoline Slicer performing at its peak, rinse it immediately after use to prevent starch buildup in the adjustable settings.

Avoid using abrasive scrubbers on the blade, as small scratches can snag the potato and cause uneven slices. A gentle soap and a soft brush are all you need to keep those restaurant-thin results consistent for years to come.

FAQ

Can I use a food processor instead of a mandoline?

You can use a slicing disk attachment in a food processor, but it often results in uneven shapes and "shattered" edges. A mandoline provides a cleaner, circular slice that looks better and cooks more evenly.

Do I have to peel sweet potatoes before slicing?

No, peeling is optional. The skin is edible and contains a lot of fiber. Just make sure to scrub the skin well with a vegetable brush to remove any dirt before you begin slicing.

Why are my chips curling in the oven?

Curling is natural for thin slices. To minimize this, ensure you are using a parchment-lined baking sheet and don't overcrowd the pan. If they curl too much, you can gently press them down with a spatula halfway through the baking process.
